question: What rule does Burp 52685s browser crawler use to choose which links to visit? It skipped /ftp/legal.md and /ftp/announcement_encrypted.md on Juice Shop and followed no links on a plain test site.
probes: Capture the crawler browser traffic and DevTools events during a crawl (Burp crawl logging_directory option)
Vary Content-Type and Content-Disposition of linked downloads in the test site
resolution: RESOLVED (2026-11-16): the rule is Burp's crawl strategy (enum burp.Zmqs, default NORMAL). Its link-pruning tolerances (unmatchedAnchorTolerance=2, total unmatched actions 2, URL-action masking threshold 1, maxLocationsPerUrl=10) make the crawler skip links whose action descriptors match ones already explored. /ftp/legal.md and /ftp/announcement_encrypted.md fall under that. An uncapped fresh-project Burp crawl of Juice visits the same 21 locations, so the 10-minute cap was not the cause. The 'no links on a plain test site' observation came from the legacy crawler (browser disabled as root). See fnd_82. WebProbe follows every link (a superset); porting the masking itself needs the crawl-graph engine (net.portswigger.crawlgraph), which is not decompiled.
